newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: IMPORT DEMAND, SPECULATION POUND ZIMBABWE DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: IMPORT DEMAND, SPECULATION POUND ZIMBABWE DOLLAR.

text.p: Continuing import demand coupled with a spate of speculation in a short interbank market drove the Zimbabwe dollar more than one percent down on the key U.S. dollar on Thursday, foreign exchange dealers said.
At the end of business on Thursday, the Zimbabwe dollar had slid to 10.7200/7400 against the U.S. currency from 10.5600/5800 at Wednesday's close.

"A loss of 1.4 percent in one day is just not healthy at all," one dealer said, adding the central Reserve Bank and the Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association were meeting later in the day to discuss the local unit's losses.

"The Reserve Bank is concerned but that concern didn't translate into much support for the (Zimbabwe) dollar... The Bank came in but didn't provide much, maybe because it wanted to prevent people quoting wide margins," another one said.
Reserve Bank officials were not available for comment.

"If nothing positive comes out of the meeting we might see people quoting wide spreads tomorrow to protect themselves because the indications are that the market is grossly oversold," said one dealer.

The dealers said although it was widely acknowledged that the Zimbabwe dollar was overvalued, they were worried at the pace at which it was losing ground against the currencies of its major trading partners.

On the crosses on Thursday, the local unit tumbled to 17.0130/0550 on sterling from 16.7510/7920 and weakened to 6.9670/9810 on the mark from 6.8570/8730. It also lost ground to the rand, against which it was quoted at 2.3530/3590.
